title: Braided-regions failover and session propagation for hosted API gateway
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: The hosted API edge must remain available and within SLOs during partial region outages or capacity loss, while preserving session and streaming continuity where possible. Current routing favors single-region affinity and simple fail-closed behavior which causes connection tears and client-visible errors during churn. Goals: (1) design a braided-regions active-active failover pattern that shifts traffic incrementally across regions while maintaining p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs, (2) ensure streaming sessions (server-sent and WebSocket) either continue with minimal reconnects or provide graceful degraded responses, (3) implement circuit breakers and load-shedding rules that protect downstream GPU pools and error budgets, (4) provide observable runbooks and automated rollback triggers. Scope: hosted API edge/gateway, session affinity strategies, streaming reconnection patterns, circuit breaker thresholds, load-shedding policies, telemetry and runbook for incident response.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic multi-region failover test reproduces a region outage and shifts 100% traffic to secondary region with <= 1% increase in p99 latency over baseline and no more than 0.5% additional error rate.

Streaming sessions: for long-lived streams (>=60s) 90% of streams reconnect automatically and resume within 5s without duplicate tokens/outputs; remaining 10% fail with clear error code and safe fallback.
Circuit breaker engages when 5xx rate > 0.5% for 30s or when tail latency > 2x baseline p99 and triggers traffic reroute and alerting.
Load-shedding policy reduces non-critical batch/embedding requests first and keeps critical interactive requests within configured latency SLOs during degraded operation.
Dashboard and runbook in Console with token-level error budgets, per-region capacity metrics, and automated rollback anchor (global traffic cutover to baseline region) are created and tested.
Design doc and a runtime PR implementing the routing policy and breaker logic merged with end-to-end tests and chaos test coverage.

decisions: Adopt braided weight-shifting: move traffic in 5% increments with 30s observation window between steps; if p99 increases > 10% or 5xx rate > 0.2% revert one step.

Session propagation: include deterministic session key (X-RW-Session) at edge; use consistent hashing to prefer original region but allow secondary region to accept connections when primary signals degraded.

Streaming behavior: prefer reconnect-and-resume pattern. For server-sent and WebSocket streams maintain a short-lived relay (stale-forward) for 3s to absorb flapping, then instruct client to reconnect with last-ack token.

Circuit breaker thresholds: trip soft-breaker at 0.5% 5xx across 30s sliding window (alert only), hard-breaker at 2% 5xx or GPU queue depth > 80% (actively redistribute traffic and mark region degraded).

Load-shedding priority: drop/queue non-interactive batch/embedding requests first, switch to quantized/smaller model variants for degraded throughput, preserve interactive chat/generation traffic until SLO violation.
Telemetry: expose per-token and per-connection traces to Console. Error budget burn by route and region is the primary gating signal for roll-forward/rollback decisions.
Runbook: automated rollback (global traffic weight reset to baseline region) must be executable via Console and have a human-confirmation step if >30% traffic impacted.
